 Marvel reveals the name of its new Iron Man , who barely resembles the human billionaire beneath the red-and-gold suit of armor. Every superhero name can turn into a mantle that can be passed on to a new generation, and even Thor's given name has become an inheritable title. However, few Avengers are as closely tied to their superhero moniker as Tony Stark, who has yet to see a different hero take up the "Iron Man" mantle. While Rhodey Rhodes and Doctor Doom have replaced Iron Man temporarily in the comics and Riri Williams has inherited his legacy as Ironheart, Tony Stark has always been Iron Man.

 It's in Tony Stark's nature to make Iron Man the Avenger who evolves the most. The leap from Iron Man's first gold and silver models to the now-iconic red-and-gold suits is one of the biggest displays of reinvention from a Marvel hero. Years later, it became common for Stark to arrive casually to the battlefield wearing Hulkbuster, Thorbuster, and even Galactus-buster suits of Iron Man armor . Other upgrades like nanotech, Extremis, Endo-Sym, and holographic technology have revolutionized Iron Man in recent years.
 Sometimes, it's not Tony Stark who leads Iron Man to evolve, but an external force so great that the Armored Avenger transforms into an unrecognizable creature.
 The Infernal Hulk's Mutated Iron Man Gets An Official Name
 The Infernal Hulk Transforms Iron Man Into 'The Iron Thing'
 The Infernal Hulk assembles his team of monster Avengers 
 Hulk War’s character sheet of the Infernal Hulk’s monster Avengers 
 Close The Infernal Hulk assembles his team of monster Avengers 
 Hulk War’s character sheet of the Infernal Hulk’s monster Avengers 
 Marvel teased the Infernal Hulk's team for the upcoming Hulk War since May, but it's only until now does Marvel reveal the names of the monstrous Avengers. The Infernal Hulk's first recruit is Iron Man, who fell despite wielding a spear linked to the One Above All and wearing the overpowered Hellbuster armor . After transforming into a misshapen creature even bigger and bulkier than the Hulk himself, Iron Man cements himself as "The Iron Thing", potentially the Infernal Hulk's right-hand man in Marvel's Hulk War event.
 Iron Man's "Iron Thing" moniker sounds like a deliberate insult from the Infernal Hulk. The typically vain and brilliant Tony Stark is now the most horrifying creature in the Infernal Hulk's army, with nothing but a simple gray mask to hide his face. Unlike Ben Grimm, Tony Stark isn't accustomed to seeing his body transformed into a colossal mass of muscle, let alone lose control over it. Iron Man's high-tech gear is gone, and his intellect is forcefully limited so his brute force can become his main asset.
 Iron Man's Iron Thing Transformation Is Still Less Painful Than Other Two Avengers'
 Spider-Man And Captain America Seem To Be In Even More Pain
 Spider-Man becomes a spider monster in Infernal Hulk 
 The Iron Thing is certainly the largest and most visibly strong member of the Infernal Hulk's monstrous Avengers, but even though his body is inorganically asymmetrical and clearly painful to maneuver, Iron Man doesn't appear to be suffering as much as Spider-Man a.k.a. the Arthropod and Captain America a.k.a. The War Dead. The Arthropod spider bursts straight out of Spider-Man's abdomen , leaving Peter Parker hanging from the giant arachnid's belly, while The War Dead is simply a crucified Captain America being carried by four undead soldiers.

 Captain Marvel and Jubilee are perhaps the luckiest Avengers in the Infernal Hulk's team. Carol Danvers transforms into a skull-faced avian creature that resembles a more horror-inspired version of Betty Ross' Harpy and Red Harpy forms, and Jubilee becomes a glowing entity made of pure energy. Vision lies in the middle, having transformed into a huge brain wrapped inside a robotic body without a face, but with a huge eye in the middle, and supported by wings, like an angel.
